classified_spans.text:
## System Architecture

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    subgraph Agents[Agent Domains]
        A1[LPAR Agent]
        A2[Container Agent]
        A3[Address Space Agent]
        A4[AI Accelerator Agent]
    end

    subgraph Fabric[Zero-Trust Agent Fabric]
        GW[Communication Gateway]
        TE[Trust Evaluator]
        SC[Security Challenge Engine]
        TS[Trust Score Calculator]
        PE[Policy Enforcer]
    end

    subgraph Context[Security Context Sources]
        RACF[RACF Permissions]
        WC[Workload Classifications]
        DSL[Data Sensitivity Labels]
        RA[Runtime Attestations]
    end

    subgraph Actions[Enforcement Actions]
        ALLOW[Allow Communication]
        RESTRICT[Restrict Scope]
        QUARANTINE[Quarantine Agent]
        DENY[Deny Communication]
    end

    subgraph Audit[Audit Trail]
        TDL[Trust Decision Log]
        IL[Interaction Log]
    end

    A1 & A2 & A3 & A4 --> GW
    GW --> TE
    RACF & WC & DSL & RA --> TE
    TE --> SC
    SC --> TS
    TS --> PE
    PE --> ALLOW
    PE --> RESTRICT
    PE --> QUARANTINE
    PE --> DENY
    PE --> TDL
    PE --> IL
```

## Sequence Diagram

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant AA as Requesting Agent
    participant GW as Fabric Gateway
    participant TE as Trust Evaluator
    participant RACF as RACF / Context Sources
    participant SC as Challenge Engine
    participant TS as Trust Scorer
    participant PE as Policy Enforcer
    participant BA as Target Agent
    participant AL as Audit Log

    AA->>GW: Request to invoke Target Agent
    GW->>TE: Evaluate security context
    TE->>RACF: Query permissions and labels
    RACF-->>TE: RACF perms, workload class, sensitivity
    TE->>SC: Issue dynamic security challenge
    SC->>AA: Challenge identity and environment
    AA-->>SC: Challenge response with attestation
    SC->>TS: Compute trust score
    TS->>PE: Trust score and context
    alt Trust score sufficient
        PE->>BA: Authorize communication
        BA-->>AA: Response
        PE->>AL: Log ALLOW decision
    else Trust score degraded
        PE->>AA: Restrict or deny communication
        PE->>AL: Log RESTRICT or DENY decision
    end
```

## Trust Evaluation Flow

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    subgraph Identity[Identity Validation]
        IV1[Agent ID Verification]
        IV2[Credential Freshness Check]
    end

    subgraph Authorization[Authorization Check]
        AZ1[RACF Permission Lookup]
        AZ2[Workload Classification Match]
        AZ3[Data Sensitivity Clearance]
    end

    subgraph Environment[Environment Attestation]
        EA1[Execution Domain Integrity]
        EA2[Runtime State Validation]
    end

    subgraph Scoring[Trust Scoring]
        CALC[Score Aggregation]
        THR[Threshold Evaluation]
    end

    subgraph Outcome[Decision]
        PASS[Trust Established]
        FAIL[Trust Denied]
        DEG[Trust Degraded]
    end

    IV1 & IV2 --> CALC
    AZ1 & AZ2 & AZ3 --> CALC
    EA1 & EA2 --> CALC
    CALC --> THR
    THR --> PASS
    THR --> FAIL
    THR --> DEG
```

## Continuous Re-evaluation State Diagram

```mermaid
stateDiagram-v2
    [*] --> Unauthenticated
    Unauthenticated --> Challenging: Agent requests communication
    Challenging --> Trusted: Challenge passed, high trust score
    Challenging --> Restricted: Challenge passed, marginal score
    Challenging --> Denied: Challenge failed
    Trusted --> Challenging: Periodic re-evaluation triggered
    Trusted --> Restricted: Anomalous behavior detected
    Trusted --> Quarantined: Trust score drops critically
    Restricted --> Challenging: Re-challenge issued
    Restricted --> Quarantined: Further degradation
    Quarantined --> Challenging: Admin review and reset
    Denied --> Unauthenticated: Session terminated
    Quarantined --> Denied: Quarantine timeout exceeded
```

TASK: Create mermaid.js diagrams for this invention. INSTRUCTION: Output ONLY mermaid code blocks. No explanations. MERMAID RULES (for PNG / mermaid-cli compatibility): - Do NOT use HTML line breaks in the diagram: no

They break many renderers and image export. - Use shorter labels, multiple nodes, or subgraphs instead of forcing line breaks inside one label. INVENTION: --- invention-id: invention-20260622-110511 company: IBM created: 2026-06-22T11:05:17 --- # Invention Idea As autonomous agents become deployed across mainframe environments, trust is often inherited from the surrounding infrastructure rather than continuously validated. We propose a Zero-Trust Agent Fabric that governs all agent-to-agent communication within the mainframe, regardless of whether agents execute in LPARs, containers, address spaces, or AI accelerator domains. Before an agent can invoke another agent, the fabric evaluates security context derived from RACF permissions, workload classifications, data sensitivity labels, and runtime attestations. Rather than relying solely on static credentials, the fabric dynamically issues security challenges that validate an agent's current identity, authorization, execution environment, and operational state. Trust is therefore established per interaction and continuously re-evaluated as agents perform work. The system can automatically restrict, quarantine, or deny communications when trust scores degrade or anomalous behavior is detected. This creates a mainframe-native zero-trust architecture for autonomous agents that reduces lateral movement risks while providing a complete audit trail of agent trust decisions and interactions. OUTPUT: ## System Architecture `mermaid flowchart TD subgraph Input[Data Sources] A[Source A] B[Source B] end subgraph Process[Processing] C[Tracker] D[Detector] end subgraph Output[Results] E[Clean Data] F[Alerts] end A --> C B --> C C --> D D --> E D --> F ` ## Sequence Diagram `mermaid sequenceDiagram participant S as Source participant T as Tracker participant D as Detector participant Sys as System S->>T: Submit Data T->>D: Validate D->>Sys: Forward or Block ` Create diagrams specific to THIS invention.
